parts.label: The two panels
parts.title: A strip and a square
parts.body: The strip: 1 ft 6 in by 2 in. The square: 6 in by 6 in. Each gold sheet: 1 in by 1 in.

think.script:
Hello, mathematicians! Today we're stepping into a real workshop: Leonardo da Vinci's, in Milan, more than five hundred years ago.

[ON SCREEN: The workshop jobs]

Leonardo painted pictures and built machines, and before he painted anything, he measured it. After the warm-up, you'll find a board with six workshop jobs for today.

[ON SCREEN: The two panels]

Here's the first puzzle. Two panels need gold. One is a long, thin strip, 1 foot 6 inches long and 2 inches wide. The other is a square, 6 inches on each side. Each gold sheet is a square, 1 inch on every side. Bernardo thinks the long strip needs way more gold.

Look at the two panels before you do anything. What do you notice? What do you wonder? Look at the units, too. Write that down, then make a guess and hold on to it. Then find out your own way. On the Lesson tab, the Math Crew will show you their ways.

learn.label: Lesson · the Crew's ways: same units first, or split where the units change
learn.title: Two Ways, One Answer
learn.where: Lesson tab, top (before the Math Crew card)
learn.script:
Welcome back. Let's look at the strip again. What's different about its two sides? One is in feet and inches, and one is in inches. Hmm.

[ON SCREEN: Live: the tile grid]
[DO: lay a row of 18 tiles along the top, then a second row under it]

The gold sheets are 1 inch on every side, so I'll put inches on both sides. 1 foot is 12 inches, and 6 more is 18. Watch: one row of 18 sheets, and a second row. 2 rows of 18. 18 times 2 is 36.

[ON SCREEN: The Crew's ways]

That's Atlas's way: same units first. Felix splits the strip at the 1-foot mark. 12 times 2 is 24, 6 times 2 is 12, and 24 plus 12 is 36. Same answer. Hazel pictures the square: 6 rows of 6. And Cora checks the units before anyone multiplies.

Pause here. Say out loud which way is more like what you did.

Here's the big idea: area is always in square units, so the sides must be in the same unit before you multiply. Now read the Crew's ways, and then try your first job.

parts.label: Problem 2
parts.title: A rug: 3 yd by 2 ft
parts.body: Express the area in square feet.

do.script:
Let's do a few together.

[ON SCREEN: Live: problem 1]
[DO: build a rectangle 14 tiles long and 2 tiles wide]

Problem 1: a gold strip 1 foot 2 inches long and 2 inches wide. Are the lengths in the same units? No. 1 foot 2 inches is 14 inches. 14 times 2 is 28 square inches.

[ON SCREEN: Problem 2]
[DRAW: a rectangle; write 3 yd on top and 2 ft on the side, then 9 ft above 3 yd]

Your turn first. Pause the video and try this one on paper. Then press play and check. A rug 3 yards long and 2 feet wide, in square feet. 1 yard is 3 feet, so 3 yards is 9 feet. 9 times 2 is 18 square feet.

[ON SCREEN: Watch out]
[DRAW: circle the 1 ft and the 7 in, then write 12 × 7 = 84]

Someone wrote 1 times 7 is 7. The times table is right, but the units are mixed. Change 1 foot to 12 inches. 12 times 7 is 84 square inches. Ask it every time: are the lengths in the same units?

parts.label: The big question
parts.title: Different units?
parts.body: Put both sides in the same unit first. Then length × width.

wrap.script:
You did it. Not one sheet of the Duke's gold was wasted.

[ON SCREEN: The big question]

So, how can you find the area when the sides use different units? Change them to the same unit first, usually the smaller one, like feet to inches or yards to feet. Then multiply length times width, and write your answer in square units.

Next time, the Duke wants a panel that uses exactly 48 gold sheets and is 4 inches wide. How long must it be? That's Area of Rectangles, Part 2. See you in the workshop.
